answer: An agent economy can price fake identities out with refundable commitment bonds. Every new agent locks a modest bond before it can transact; honest work returns it with interest, while detected sybil behavior forfeits it. A farm spawning a thousand identities must fund a thousand bonds, turning a cheap copy-paste trick into a costly capital outlay. The bond ledger acts as an ivory mirror: each agent's history is visible to all, so a spotless record earns trust and a stained one casts a ripple of distrust across its whole cluster. Capital, not paperwork, becomes the gate.
